title: Second Swedish Crusade
description: Birger Jarl leads a Swedish expedition into Tavastia, binding south-western Finland to the Swedish crown; some historians date it to 1238 or 1239.

title: Treaty of Nöteborg
description: Sweden and Novgorod fix their border for the first time, dividing Karelia between them.

title: Helsinki founded
description: Gustav I of Sweden founds a trading town to compete with Tallinn across the gulf.

title: Royal Academy of Turku founded
description: Queen Christina's government founds Finland's first university, which moves to Helsinki in 1828.

title: Great Famine
description: Failed harvests kill about a third of the population of Finland.

title: Treaty of Nystad
description: Ending the Great Northern War, Sweden cedes its Baltic provinces and south-eastern Finland with Vyborg to Russia; the date is New Style.

title: Building of Sveaborg begins
description: Sweden starts a sea fortress off Helsinki to guard against Russia.

title: Diet of Porvoo
description: The estates of Finland swear allegiance to Alexander I, who promises to keep their laws and religion, making Finland a grand duchy under the Russian emperor.

title: Treaty of Fredrikshamn
description: Sweden cedes Finland to Russia, ending six centuries of Swedish rule.

title: Helsinki made the capital
description: Alexander I moves the capital of the grand duchy from Turku to Helsinki.

title: Kalevala published
description: Elias Lönnrot publishes his compilation of Karelian and Finnish folk poetry, which becomes the national epic.

title: Diet reconvened
description: Alexander II calls the Diet of Finland for the first time since 1809, and it meets regularly from then on.

title: Famine of 1866 to 1868
description: The last great famine of northern Europe kills roughly 150,000 people, about 8.5% of the population.

title: February Manifesto
description: Nicholas II asserts the right to rule Finland without the consent of its Diet, beginning the first period of Russification.

title: Universal suffrage
description: A single-chamber parliament replaces the Diet, and Finnish women become the first in Europe to gain the vote, along with the right to stand for election.

title: Declaration of independence
description: Parliament adopts the declaration of independence from Russia.

title: Civil War begins
description: Red Guards take Helsinki and the south; the Whites, with German help, win the war by May.

title: Battle of Tampere ends
description: The Whites take the Reds' main stronghold in the largest battle of the Civil War.

title: Republican constitution
description: After a failed plan for a German-born king, Finland adopts a constitution as a republic.

title: Treaty of Tartu
description: Finland and Soviet Russia settle their border, and Finland gains Petsamo on the Arctic Ocean.

title: Winter War begins
description: The Soviet Union attacks Finland, which holds out for three and a half months.

title: Moscow Peace Treaty
description: Finland ends the Winter War by ceding Karelia with Vyborg, about a tenth of its territory.

title: Continuation War begins
description: After Soviet air raids Finland declares itself at war, fighting beside Germany to regain the land lost in 1940.

title: Moscow Armistice
description: Finland leaves the war, accepting the 1940 border, the loss of Petsamo and heavy reparations.

title: Treaty of friendship with the Soviet Union
description: The agreement keeps Finland outside the Soviet bloc in return for a pledge not to let its territory be used against the Soviet Union.

title: Helsinki Olympics
description: The Summer Olympics open in Helsinki, twelve years after the games planned there were cancelled.

title: Helsinki Accords
description: Thirty-five states of East and West sign the Final Act of the Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe.

title: Finland joins the European Union
description: Finland becomes a member together with Austria and Sweden.
